alerts.title: DTG-associated hyperglycemia: pre-diabetes developed
alerts.message: Guidelines require screening for hyperglycemia risk before DTG use and state that known diabetics or those with high blood glucose should not initiate or transition to DTG. DTG has been reported to cause hyperglycemia in previously non-diabetic adults. Since starting DTG 18 months ago, this patient developed impaired fasting glucose (118 mg/dL, up from baseline 92) and pre-diabetic HbA1c (6.1%). She also gained 17 kg and has acanthosis nigricans. Evidence for drug attribution: DTG is a known cause of hyperglycemia, and the onset temporally follows DTG initiation. Evidence against: Family history of diabetes and obesity are independent risk factors. Guidelines recommend glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year after DTG initiation, which appears overdue.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess for diabetes; consider switching to a metabolically neutral ARV (ABC, TAF-based). Reinstate glucose monitoring every 3 months. Refer for diabetes prevention counseling including weight management.

alerts.title: Significant weight gain on DTG with metabolic consequences
alerts.message: Guidelines list rapid weight gain as a risk factor for developing diabetes in PLHIV and recommend weight management for at-risk patients. This patient gained 17 kg (65 to 82 kg) with BMI rising from 25.6 to 32.4 kg/m² within 18 months of switching to DTG. Waist circumference is 96 cm. DTG is associated with significant weight gain. The weight gain has coincided with new-onset pre-diabetes, dyslipidemia, and elevated blood pressure, compounding cardiovascular risk. Guidelines recommend prescribing metabolically neutral ARVs (ABC, TDF, 3TC) for patients at risk of developing DM.

evidence.recommended_action: Consider switching DTG to a metabolically neutral regimen. Initiate structured weight loss counseling including diet, exercise, and smoking cessation if applicable.

alerts.title: Missing clinician assessment and plan for abnormal labs
alerts.message: Guidelines require clinician assessment when adverse events are suspected on DTG, including checking glucose and clinical management based on symptoms and signs. The DTG monitoring flowchart triggers assessment for weight changes and symptoms interfering with daily activities. This patient reports weight gain and fatigue with abnormal glucose, HbA1c, and lipids, yet no assessment or plan was documented. Required actions include diabetes screening, lipid management evaluation, and blood pressure follow-up. The treatment goal for blood pressure is <140/90 mmHg; this patient is at 138/88 mmHg, borderline.

evidence.recommended_action: Document clinical assessment addressing weight gain, fatigue, pre-diabetes, dyslipidemia, and borderline BP. Order follow-up fasting glucose and lipid panel. Provide lifestyle counseling.

alerts.title: New-onset dyslipidemia with atherogenic profile
alerts.message: Guidelines identify dyslipidemia as a risk factor for diabetes in PLHIV and recommend weight management and lifestyle modification. This patient has total cholesterol 228 mg/dL, LDL 148 mg/dL, HDL 38 mg/dL, and triglycerides 212 mg/dL, all abnormal. No baseline lipids are available for comparison, but the current profile is atherogenic. DTG and TDF can contribute to lipid changes, though dietary and genetic factors may also play a role. Combined with obesity, pre-diabetes, and family history of diabetes, this significantly increases cardiovascular risk. No lipid management plan was documented.

evidence.recommended_action: Evaluate for secondary causes. Initiate therapeutic lifestyle changes. Consider statin therapy per cardiovascular risk assessment. Repeat lipid panel in 3 months.
